name: Agent Autoloop
cost: Free (MIT). Model usage is billed to your own agent account
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, ACP agents, DeepSeek Harness and other CLI agents, on macOS and Linux
short: Runs your command line agent in the background on schedules or events, and sends you a card only when it needs a decision.
what: Agent Autoloop is a small hub that hands work to your CLI agent from schedules, GitHub or GitLab webhooks and HTTP events. The agent works one round and exits. When it needs you, for things like deleting data or spending money, it sends a card to a desktop notification, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, Slack or Discord. While it waits, no agent process runs and no tokens are spent. Your answer resumes the same conversation.
who: People who want an agent to handle recurring jobs, like a morning brief or new GitHub issues, without sitting at the terminal. Windows users should wait, since it doesn't run there yet.
needs: macOS or Linux (WSL2 for now on Windows)
At least one command line agent that is already signed in

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: The installer pipes a script from GitHub into your shell. It installs the newest release.

steps.title: Do a test run
steps.text: Your agent asks a sample question. Answer it with the number shown, then check the status.

steps.title: Write your rules
steps.text: Edit `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json` to say what job goes to which agent in which folder, for example a cron rule for a 9am brief. Then check it.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `agent-autoloop try`, pick a color when the card asks, then run `agent-autoloop status` to see the agent pick the work back up, with rounds, tokens and cost for today.

watch: The install command pipes a script straight into your shell. Read install.sh first.
It runs your signed-in agent unattended. The README says providers generally recommend API keys over personal subscriptions for automated work, and model usage is billed to your account.
CLI output, default notifications and the recipe docs are in Chinese for now.
Windows is not supported yet. The author plans it after 7 to 8 November.
